KEY MESSAGE 1...No significant changes in forecast thinking for
the weekend. Cloudy but warm conditions are noted across ENC 
this afternoon as moisture continues to stream N'wards out ahead
of a N'ward moving front and its associated complex low 
pressure system. Have already seen some showers approach the 
coast and scattered light showers are forecast to increase in 
coverage through the afternoon and evening. 

Otherwise as noted above, complex low pressure system 
consisting of multiple lows currently reside along a slowly 
moving warm front stretching from the FL/GA border to north of 
the Bahamas this afternoon. Shortwave energy lifting out of the 
Georgia will aid in lifting the low pressure system northward 
tonight through Sunday. Most guidance continues to converge on 
a solution of the low north of the Bahamas becoming the 
dominate low as it lifts northward off the coast. However, some
AI models continue to show the primary low remaining closer to 
the Southeast coast and tracking across ENC. While this 
continues to bring some uncertainty with the details of the 
forecast, there is not significant changes with the latest 
forecast package. 

The greatest impacts with this system are expected along the
coast where large surf, beach erosion, and minor ocean overwash
will be possible with the contribution of high astronomical 
tides adding to the impacts. As a matter of fact, given the 
concerns about ocean overwash, ended up issuing a coastal flood
advisory across Hatteras Island which begins tonight and 
continues into Sunday morning to capture the peak of the high 
surf advisory that is currently out across portions of the OBX. 
As of right now, any potential minor ocean overwash would be 
relegated to the most vulnerable dune structures along Hwy 12 
on Hatteras Island. Still think coastal flooding impacts across 
the sounds and rivers will be minimal at best giving the weaker 
winds, but given the developing King Tides, there may be minor 
inundation for locations adjacent to the sounds and rivers.

Rainfall amounts continue to trend lower as ENC looks to remain
between the two areas of ascent with much of ENC now only 
forecast to see 0.25-0.75" of rain this weekend from these 
systems. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...The King Tide Cycle starts tomorrow and peaks
middle of next week. This higher than normal astronomical tide 
cycle is slightly stronger than the one that occurred the last 
week of OCT. The tide levels may be exacerbated by a series of 
low pressure systems that are expected to impact the region over
the next week. 

The first system is currently impacting the area this weekend, 
however latest guidance looks to keep any impacts from this
system rather weak in nature. However, this system will produce
large surf along the coast and the higher than normal tides may
help contribute to some minor ocean overwash around times of 
high tide, especially where the dune structure is compromised
along Hatteras Island.

Another potentially stronger low pressure system is expected to
impact the area around the middle of next week. The strength 
and track of this low will determine where the greatest impacts
will occur, but most tidal locations across ENC should expect 
elevated water levels with at least minor to moderate impacts 
across the typical vulnerable areas. Interests along the coast 
should watch the forecast closely over the next week for the 
potential for greater impacts, especially as it has to potential
to impact holiday travel.

KEY MESSAGE 3...Once again no real changes to the forecast in
the long term as guidance continues to suggest strong high
pressure builds in from the north early next week. A deepening 
trough then moves through the Gulf states and progresses 
offshore of the SE US with a surface low developing along the 
coast or just off the coast near the Gulf Stream. This low then
deepens as it lifts northward off the coast Wednesday into 
Thursday. Upper level support is greater with this system and 
high pressure to the north will be stronger which will likely 
bring a tighter pressure gradient across the area resulting in 
stronger winds. While there remains uncertainty with the exact 
details with this system, it will have the potential to bring 
greater impacts across the area, especially along the coast and 
tidal locations as it will coincide with the peak of King Tides 
bringing a greater risk of coastal flooding, beach erosion, and 
ocean overwash. This system will also have the potential to 
bring impacts to holiday travel on Wednesday and Thursday.
